name: BNL-E-0816
summary: BNL E816 searched for electron-flavour appearance in the Brookhaven AGS neutrino beam using a fine-grained calorimeter. It reported a modest electron-like event excess whose statistical significance did not establish oscillations.
physics_targets: Short-baseline muon-to-electron neutrino and antineutrino appearance
Electron and photon separation in neutrino interactions
detection_principle: Flash-tube tracking planes interleaved with iron and downstream shower-absorber material reconstruct electromagnetic showers. Fine sampling distinguishes electrons emerging from the neutrino vertex from photons converting after a measurable gap; scintillator hodoscopes provide the trigger.

status.label: Completed / historical
status.evidence: The final historical analysis is published in Nuclear Physics B335 (1990).

key_parameters.name: Target-to-detector distance
key_parameters.value: 175 m; approximately 130 m from the decay-tunnel midpoint

key_parameters.name: Calorimeter dimensions
key_parameters.value: Approximately 6 m wide, 3 m high and 3.3 m long

key_parameters.name: Analysis fiducial mass
key_parameters.value: 7 tonnes in the selected interaction region

key_parameters.name: Flux peak
key_parameters.value: Approximately 0.8 GeV in the original beam calculation

results.summary: Electron-like events were approximately twice the beam-composition expectation, with only about two-standard-deviation significance. This was not a confirmed neutrino-oscillation observation.

science_scope: The Brookhaven E816 apparatus is distinct from CERN PS191 even though the programmes shared participants and scientific motivation. Baseline conventions are stated explicitly rather than confusing target distance with decay-midpoint distance.
